PullRequest.Title: [Perf] sessions: coalesce catalogue-driven list refreshes
PullRequest.Body:

Stacked on #343601. This PR contains only the runtime list-refresh follow-up; retarget to `main` after the shutdown fix lands.

Coalesce provider/catalogue invalidations and related host-filter updates into one Sessions list render per animation frame. Provider/model notifications remain synchronous. Concrete session additions, removals and edits, plus explicit refresh/update calls, still render immediately so move/reveal feedback is preserved.

Measured in isolated Code OSS restoring a real cached profile with 613 sessions and 253–254 providers/backends, with development-only disposable tracking disabled. Interleaved original/candidate runs:

| Measurement | Original | Follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List updates | 764–769 | 136–137 |
| Average time in list-update code | 2.80 s | 0.54 s |
| Average time until full catalogue/list settled | 14.16 s | 10.97 s |

A separate comparison verified identical complete tree composition, ordering, collapse state and session identities. Unchanged inventory updates were already cheap (~1 ms, no list refresh); single-host status/label changes still produce one update within the same observed paint window. These are local cached-startup results, not a claim of faster network discovery or the same benefit for empty/small profiles.

To test manually, reload an Agents window with a populated cached remote-host/session inventory. Check that the list settles faster while selection, keyboard focus, grouping, and drag-and-drop feedback remain intact.

Nine regressions cover burst coalescing, focus/selection, immediate concrete deltas and explicit refreshes, hidden-list restoration, disposal, and reentrant invalidation.

<details>

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob '**/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/*.test.js'` — 975 passed.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --browser webkit --reporter dot --runGlob '**/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/*.test.js'` — 974 passed in Chromium and 974 passed in WebKit.

(Written by Copilot)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each provider/backend catalogue notification synchronously rebuilt the entire sessions tree, and one registration also fans out into related management and host-filter notifications. Startup catalogue hydration therefore repeated O(session-count) filtering/grouping/allocation and DOM-tree reconciliation for a provider-count-sized burst.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Populated cached profiles incurred repeated full-list rendering during catalogue hydration, increasing startup settling latency and main-thread CPU/GC pressure.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed provider listener calls scheduleListUpdate(), which keeps one animation-frame disposable and merges related provider, host-filter, and empty catalogue invalidations; update() clears the queued work so an authoritative immediate render also cancels a redundant pending render.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, the provider-catalogue listener at line 4275 synchronously called SessionsList.update() for every onDidChangeProviders event. SessionsProvidersService fires that event once per provider/backend registration, AgentHostFilterService synchronously recomputes and may emit a related host-filter invalidation for the same registration, and SessionsManagementService emits a related session-catalogue event. SessionsList.update() performs collection-wide filtering/grouping/sorting, constructs the full tree input, and calls tree.setChildren. The added test drives 125 interleaved provider/catalogue/host invalidations and proves the changed path performs one session read and one update after a frame rather than one render per notification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a populated cached Sessions profile while hundreds of providers/backends register and related catalogue/host-filter notifications fire.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider registration synchronously updates management and host-filter state; visible-list progress now waits for at most one scheduled animation-frame callback, which performs one full SessionsList update for all same-frame invalidations. Provider/model notifications themselves remain synchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collection-wide session filtering/grouping/sorting/allocation followed by WorkbenchObjectTree.setChildren DOM/tree reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One render per animation frame after coalescing, rather than one render for each provider, empty catalogue, and host-filter notification; effective session cardinality is the full visible inventory after filtering and grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every relevant notification synchronously rebuilt the full tree; the diff reduces those calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single frame callback is on the visible list's settling path, but replaces many synchronous UI-thread renders with one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One-time legacy read-state persistence for qualifying sessions during a true refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per qualifying legacy session because migrated IDs are retained; warm/current profiles perform only in-memory guard checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration loop ran in every refresh before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the refreshed tree is built, but is pre-existing and the PR reduces repeated refresh entry during catalogue bursts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Provider/backend notification count controls pre-fix repetition; session/chat/group count controls each tree rebuild. Same-frame provider, management, and host-filter notifications deduplicate to one render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All notification handling and tree rebuilding is serialized on the UI thread. MutableDisposable permits only one pending animation-frame callback per list; refreshPending merges refresh requirements into that callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider getSessions calls consume synchronous provider-held inventories; cold/empty profiles have little tree work, while warm populated profiles scale with cached sessions. The scheduler is a one-frame coalescing cache with no key partition and is cleared by any authoritative update; hidden views defer to a full refresh when shown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener call paths, update's full-tree reconciliation, and the 125-event coalescing test directly establish multiplicity and serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame savings depend on how provider registrations are distributed across animation frames and profile size, but the repeated full-tree mechanism and its removal are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This is a concrete repeated-render performance fix, recorded separately with introducing commit attribution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change a remote host's status/label or select a different host while the Sessions list is visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentHostFilterService synchronously recomputes in-memory host entries and emits onDidChange; the list render is deferred to the next animation frame and only the latest selected-host/provider scope is rendered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full Sessions tree filter/group/reconciliation after host scope changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-list update per frame regardless of same-frame host invalidation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each host-filter notification immediately rebuilt the full list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds at most one frame before the scoped tree appears while removing repeated main-thread rendering; network reconnect/disconnect operations are not called on this event path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with visible sessions and host invalidation frequency; effective update cardinality is one per frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI-thread serialized recomputation with one pending frame callback; repeated observable changes within a frame coalesce.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No remote read or cache lookup is added. The list reads current in-memory hosts and sessions at callback time, so intermediate states require no retained snapshots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed listener directly schedules through the single MutableDisposable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host-status burst frequency varies by provider, but the callback bound is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; work is bounded and reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add, remove, edit, move, or explicitly refresh sessions while a list update is queued.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Concrete session deltas and explicit refresh/update calls synchronously read the latest in-memory session inventory and rebuild the tree so move/reveal feedback is not delayed; update clears any earlier queued frame callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the in-memory aggregate session inventory, rebuild observers, and reconcile the full tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate render per concrete delta event or explicit operation; any earlier coalesced invalidation is canceled. This is unchanged for concrete deltas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Concrete deltas and explicit refreshes also synchronously refreshed and rendered before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains deliberately on the interaction critical path to preserve move/reveal feedback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each intentional concrete event scales with full session/tree size; no new multiplicity is introduced by the scheduler.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serialized UI work. A prior queued callback is canceled; reentrant invalidation raised during rendering schedules one later frame rather than nesting repeated frame callbacks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The latest provider-held session inventory is read on refresh. Pending refresh state is monotonic within a batch and reset before the refresh, while hidden lists perform a fresh read when shown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit tests cover added/removed/changed deltas, refresh, update, hidden restoration, disposal, and reentrancy.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual tree size varies, but call count equivalence and cancellation are covered directly by changed tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; required synchronous behavior is preserved and redundant queued work is canceled.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close, reload, or switch workspace while provider/backend registration disposables tear down.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Once lifecycle willShutdown is committed, provider/backend maps are still synchronously cleaned but onDidChangeProviders is not fired, so list, management, host-filter, picker, and other consumers do not rebuild during teardown. Shutdown does not wait on new asynchronous work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup remains O(provider/backend count), but consumer notification fan-out and repeated catalogue/list rebuilding are removed for each disposal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized disposal on the UI thread; no task, promise, or queue is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider maps are emptied normally; no cache entries or late registrations are retained. Vetoed shutdown leaves willShutdown false and notifications continue, while committed shutdown suppresses only observer fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lifecycle state is an in-memory boolean set only after shutdown commitment, and tests cover vetoed and committed shutdown reasons.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and cost of active consumers varies, but suppression of the event fan-out is explicit and tested with 125 providers/backends.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the change removes shutdown-time repeated work and introduces no boundary operation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced catalogue hydration, host filtering, concrete session updates, visibility/reentrancy/disposal, and shutdown teardown. Submitted no findings because the diff adds no high-confidence performance regression; it coalesces full-tree UI work and suppresses shutdown fan-out. Recorded the proven repeated-render regression fix with blame attribution.
